correctness.rationale: For finite connected vertex- and edge-transitive d-regular H, convex spectral-norm averaging over automorphisms reduces all symmetric admissible stochastic P to two edge orbits. The block matrix has modes 1−xλ and 1−xλ−2y. With zero diagonal, y=1−dx gives max{1−δx,2dx−1} where δ=min(α,2d−β), minimized by x=2/(2d+δ), y=δ/(2d+δ), SLEM=(2d−δ)/(2d+δ). At δ=0 bipartite parity enforces eigenvalue −1 for every P. Allowing holding, the three endpoint constraints and row budget reconstruct optimum 1−2α/max(β+2α,2d+α); subtraction yields strictly positive penalty iff α+β>2d. Direct independent block-matrix eigenvalue computations and 151-point feasible x-mesh agree for complete bases m=3,4,5,9; the all-H proof is analytic.
